subject: epaulette shark
title: A Shark That Walks Out of the Water and Survives Two Hours Without Oxygen

scenes.text: This shark just walked out of the ocean. On purpose.
The epaulette shark. About three feet long, and it uses its fins like legs.
When the tide drops on Australia's reef flats, its pools get cut off and the oxygen runs out.
So it climbs out and walks across the dry reef to the next pool. Up to 90 feet.
And here's the part scientists can't match: it can go two full hours with no oxygen at all. No damage.
Most animals would be dead in minutes. This shark just waits for the tide.

description:
The epaulette shark walks on its fins across exposed reef flats when the tide goes out, covering up to about 90 feet of dry ground between pools.
Florida Atlantic University and James Cook University researchers (2022) report it can survive two hours of complete anoxia, no oxygen at all, with no ill effects, at tropical temperatures where most animals would die within minutes.
What other animal would you bet could survive without oxygen? Comment below.

first_comment: Epaulette sharks are about 3 feet long, harmless to people, and live on the reef flats of the southern Great Barrier Reef, which get cut off from the sea at low tide. Which shark should we cover next?
